title: Talk it through 1.6
role: Team leader correcting a misunderstanding about prices and rules
can_do: I can correct a misunderstanding politely and precisely.
I can use relative clauses and passives to explain rules and regulations.

nodes.partner_line: I thought the discount applied to all the tours this month.
nodes.translation: Pensé que el descuento se aplicaba a todos los tours de este mes.

options.text: Let me clear that up: it applies only to the coastal tours.
I am afraid there is a small misunderstanding about that.
Actually, the discount was valid only until last week.

nodes.partner_line: Oh, I see. Which price list should I use, then?
nodes.translation: Ah, entiendo. ¿Entonces qué lista de precios debo usar?
nodes.model_reply: Please use the new list, which was published in May.

nodes.partner_line: But the old brochure shows a lower price.
nodes.translation: Pero el folleto antiguo muestra un precio más bajo.

options.text: That brochure, which is outdated, should be ignored.
On the contrary, the old price no longer applies.
That is exactly the misunderstanding. The brochure has been withdrawn.
I am afraid not. The tariff, which is set by law, is strictly regulated.
Not this one, but we can discuss the extras.
It is regulated, rather than set by us.

nodes.partner_line: I understand. Who decides these rules?

options.text: They are set by the tourism authority, which reviews them yearly.
The regulations are updated by the ministry every January.
The rules are approved by a committee, which includes the operators.

nodes.partner_line: Thanks for explaining. That is much clearer now.
nodes.translation: Gracias por explicarlo. Ahora está mucho más claro.

options.text: You are welcome. I am glad we cleared that up.
Happy to help. Do not hesitate to ask again.
No problem. I will send the correct list by email.
